diagnostic_evidence.quote: The coefficients $\alpha_i$ and $\beta_i$ are chosen such that the first four terms of the Taylor expansions coincide

issues.failure_explanation: The text asserts that the 6-factor product e^{α1 tK1}e^{β1 tK2}...e^{β3 tK2} is algebraically of order 3 given only Σα_j=1 and Σβ_j=1. Those are just the first-order consistency conditions V'(0)=K1+K2. Order 3 needs the Taylor coefficients up to t^3 to match, which gives additional non-commutative order conditions that are not imposed or verified. Generic coefficients with unit sums give only order 1, so the claim is false as stated.

failure_location.quote: with $\alpha_1+\alpha_2+ \alpha_3 = 1$, $\beta_1+\beta_2 +\beta_3 = 1$ for which the associated product formula

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the actual order conditions and concrete coefficients, or drop the example and point to the explicit V_3 of the proposition.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative construction of a 3-stage order-3 scheme is unsupported. The valid order-3 scheme appears separately in the proposition giving V_3.
issues.title: 3-stage splitting claimed to have order 3 under only the sum-to-one conditions
issues.why_classification: It is a local illustrative statement, and the substantive order-3 scheme is given correctly elsewhere, so a short edit repairs it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (or analytic contraction semigroups if the coefficients $\alpha_{j}$'s and $\beta_{j}$'s are complex)

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem of Hansen–Ostermann needs analyticity of the semigroups precisely when the splitting coefficients are complex, since e^{α tK} with complex α must be defined and bounded. The remark says the proof is 'algebraic' and extends unchanged to bi-continuous contraction semigroups. But the Koopman semigroups of flows are not analytic. The shift semigroup of x'=1 on C_b or C_0 is not even defined for complex time. Every scheme beyond Strang (V_3, U_[k], W_[k], Z_[k]) has complex coefficients, so the quoted error bounds t^{p+1}/(n^p (p+1)!) are not justified for the nonlinear-ODE Koopman setting. The algorithms also evaluate flows at complex times without any analytic-continuation or real-part argument.

failure_location.quote: it can be extended to bi-continuous contraction semigroups without changing any of arguments

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum the paper must prove an error theorem for complex-time splittings on the relevant function spaces (for example via analyticity or analytic continuation of the frozen flows), or restrict the guarantees to real-coefficient methods (Lie–Trotter and Strang).
issues.overall_effect: The advertised higher-order convergence and error bounds for flows are unsupported for all complex-coefficient schemes. The theorems on U_[k], W_[k], Z_[k] and V_3 remain valid only as algebraic-order statements.
issues.title: Error bounds for complex-coefficient splittings claimed to carry over to non-analytic bi-continuous Koopman semigroups
issues.why_classification: The higher-order error-bound claim for non-analytic Koopman semigroups is a central advertised result. Fixing it needs new analysis or a major loss of scope, because real-coefficient methods beyond order 2 are unavailable.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: has 7 terms and is of order 4, where $a= 0.324396 + 0.134586 i$.

issues.failure_explanation: For k=1 the printed formula gives a≈0.4236+0.2836i, not the listed 0.324396+0.134586i. The printed value also fails the triple-jump cancellation condition 2a^3+(1−2a)^3=0 (moduli 0.265 vs 0.203). The listed value equals 1/(2−2^{1/3}e^{2πi/3}) = e^{πi/3}/(2e^{πi/3}+2^{1/3}), so the denominator should contain 2e^{πi/(2k+1)}. As stated, the general scheme W_[k] with the printed a_k is not of order 2k+2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace a_k by e^{πi/(2k+1)}/(2e^{πi/(2k+1)}+2^{1/(2k+1)}) and check it against the listed coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: The general-k definition of W_[k] is wrong as printed. The explicit numerical coefficients are consistent with the corrected formula.
issues.title: Closed form of a_k in the triple-jump theorem contradicts its own listed value and the order condition
issues.why_classification: It is a local correction of one coefficient formula, and the method, orders and term counts are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $D(\K)$ and $(\lambda_0 I - \K)D(\K)$ are bi-dense in $X$ for some $\lambda_0 > \omega\ge 0$
where $\sigma_{i}(t,x_{i})$ solves the one-dimensional, separable equation

issues.failure_explanation: The remarks assume only that the full system has unique, global, jointly continuous solutions in Ω. They then assert that the frozen one-dimensional flows define bi-continuous contraction semigroups e^{tK_i} on C_b(Ω), and that (V(t/n))^n g → T(t)g. This needs several things that are never established. The frozen problems must have global solutions that stay in the closed Ω; global existence of the full flow does not imply this. The e^{tK_i} must be bi-continuous contractions for the topology τ. K1+K2 (resp. K1+K2+K3) on D(K1)∩D(K2) must satisfy the density and range hypotheses of the bi-continuous Chernoff theorem. The norm-limit condition on V'(0+) must hold on a bi-dense domain. None of this is verified, and the theorem is only cited. The introduction's claim of 'proving well-posedness and contraction of the splitting operators' is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State explicit hypotheses (global frozen flows in Ω, bi-continuity of each e^{tK_i}, range/density condition) and either verify them or restrict the claim to the worked examples.
issues.overall_effect: The general convergence claim σ(t,x)=lim x_n(t,x) for the coordinate-wise algorithms is unproven beyond examples where the frozen flows are explicit and global. This also applies to the three-dimensional remark.
issues.title: Chernoff product formula applied to frozen-variable splittings without verifying its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A contained set of added hypotheses and verifications, or a limited restriction of scope, gives a comparable result without new global architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: V_3 is a composition of flows, so each update must start from the most recent state. Step (2) already advanced x to x_{k+ā}, but step (4) applies the x-flow for time a·t/n to the old x_k. The composed x-time is then a instead of ā+a=1, the result is not V_3(t/n), and the order t^4/n^3 claim does not hold for the algorithm as written. Step (4) should start from x_{k+ā}; the three-dimensional appendix version does chain the updates correctly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace x_k by x_{k+ā} in step (4).
issues.overall_effect: The stated third-order two-dimensional procedure and its approximation-order claim are wrong as written.
issues.title: Third-order 2-D algorithm restarts the x-update from x_k instead of the latest x
issues.why_classification: It is a one-index correction that leaves the scheme, order and guarantee unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To compare the list of approximated coordinates obtained from our method with those computed by the RK45 method at a fixed time $t$, we apply the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) as a metric
we observe that the number of terms grows rapidly with both the dimension and the order of the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The experiments report only RMSE against an RK45 reference, with no runtime, flop count or function-evaluation comparison. RK45 serves as ground truth, not as a competitor measured for cost. The paper's own term counts (thousands of exponentials for high orders, tens of millions for N=3 at order 14) point toward high cost. Low-order Lie–Trotter RMSE values are also large (about 0.4 to 33 for Lotka–Volterra). So neither 'competitive in accuracy' nor 'more computationally efficient' is established.

failure_location.quote: the splitting method is not only competitive in accuracy but also more computationally efficient

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add cost-versus-accuracy comparisons against standard solvers, or remove the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The efficiency claim, repeated in the abstract ('accuracy and efficiency'), has no supporting evidence.
issues.title: Computational-efficiency advantage over RK45 claimed without any cost comparison
issues.why_classification: It needs new experiments or a weakening of an advertised conclusion, but the theory is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This trend confirms that increasing the number of iterations improves the accuracy of the approximation, and higher-order methods further enhance this accuracy, particularly when the number of iterations is limited.
This pattern indicates that both increasing the number of iterations and increasing the order of the method contribute to improving the approximation.

issues.failure_explanation: Setting RK45 tolerances to 1e-16, at or below double-precision machine epsilon, does not guarantee a reference accurate to 1e-12. For the chaotic Lorenz system at t=20, errors are amplified by a large factor. The tables show RMSE stalling at roughly 1e-13 to 1e-8 and even increasing with n for high orders. Examples are 12th order, 7.75E-13 → 9.32E-10 → 1.34E-09, and 14th order, 1.01E-11 → 1.41E-09 → 1.29E-08, in Lotka–Volterra, and 6th order, 7.48E-08 → 2.75E-07, in Lorenz. This contradicts the stated conclusion that more iterations always improve accuracy. The identification of the 'best' order at each n compares values at the noise floor. The quoted conclusions therefore do not follow from the data, and the observed floor is not attributed to reference or round-off error.

failure_location.quote: This choice guarantees that the RK45 approximation is sufficiently precise for meaningful comparison.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a validated high-precision reference, such as extended precision or a validated high-order solver. State that the tables are limited by a reference or round-off floor. Restrict the conclusions to regions above that floor.
issues.overall_effect: The reported trade-off between n and order, and the 'best method' selections in the three tables and in the conclusion, are unreliable.
issues.title: Conclusions drawn from RMSE tables ignore the reference-accuracy floor and contradict the data
issues.why_classification: A contained re-computation and a weakening of the interpretation suffice; the theoretical claims are unaffected.
